sections.content:
## What You'll Learn

You'll understand the full Microsoft Copilot ecosystem — where it lives, what it can do in each location, and how it compares to Claude and Gemini for everyday professional tasks. You'll also understand why Microsoft Copilot is the default AI layer for most corporate environments, even when individuals prefer other tools for personal use.

## The Copilot Ecosystem — A Map

Microsoft Copilot is not one product — it's a brand applied to AI features throughout the Microsoft ecosystem. Understanding this prevents confusion:

| Copilot | Where | Who it's for | Cost |
|---------|-------|-------------|------|
| **Copilot.microsoft.com** | Standalone web chat | Anyone | Free |
| **Copilot in Edge** | Browser sidebar | Edge users | Free |
| **Copilot in Windows** | Win+C shortcut | Windows 11 users | Free |
| **Microsoft 365 Copilot** | Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, PowerPoint | Enterprise M365 subscribers | £25-30/user/month add-on |
| **Copilot Studio** | Web app for building custom AI | Businesses building internal tools | Paid |
| **GitHub Copilot** | VS Code, JetBrains, Eclipse, Xcode | Developers | ~$10/month (AI Credits billing from June 2026) |

All of these are powered by OpenAI models (GPT-5.x and o-series) with Microsoft customisation. Understanding one gives you a foundation for all of them.

**The Microsoft-OpenAI relationship:** Microsoft invested over $13 billion in OpenAI and integrated OpenAI models throughout its product line. This is why Bing search uses AI, why Edge has a built-in AI sidebar, and why Microsoft 365 tools have AI features built in. For enterprise users, Microsoft is typically the AI provider — not because it's the best standalone tool, but because it's already inside the tools the company pays for.

## Copilot in Edge — AI Alongside Every Web Page

Copilot in Edge lives in the sidebar of the Microsoft Edge browser (pre-installed on every Windows computer). Click the Copilot icon in the top right corner or press **Ctrl+Shift+.** to open it.

**The key capability:** The sidebar is context-aware — it can see and read the page you're currently viewing. You don't copy-paste anything.

**Most useful actions on any page:**
```
"Summarise this page in 5 bullet points"
"What claims in this article should I fact-check?"
"Explain the term [jargon from the page] in plain English"
"What questions does this article leave unanswered?"
"Compare what this says to what I know about [related topic]"
"Extract all the action items or recommendations from this page"
```

**For long documents in browser:**
```
"List all the numbers/statistics in this report"
"What does this legal document require me to do?"
"Summarise the key findings for a non-expert audience"
```

**The composing panel:** A separate tab in the sidebar lets you draft content for any platform — email, LinkedIn post, blog, document. You specify the format, length, and tone, then copy the result into wherever you're writing.

**Practical workflow example:**
You're reading a long competitor's case study. Open Copilot sidebar:
1. "Summarise the key claims in this case study"
2. "What evidence do they provide for each claim?"
3. "What weaknesses or gaps do you see in their argument?"
4. Switch to Compose tab: "Draft a rebuttal to these points for our sales team"

All without leaving the page or opening another tab.

## Microsoft 365 Copilot — AI Inside Your Work Tools

For organisations that pay for Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI is woven directly into every Office application. This is significant because it meets people where they already work — they don't have to leave their document or email to use AI.

**Copilot in Word:**
- "Draft a first version of this report based on these bullet points" → produces a full draft you can edit
- "Rewrite this section in a more formal tone"
- "Summarise this 40-page document in a 1-page executive summary"
- "Is there anything important missing from this proposal?"
- Add the Copilot sidebar and ask questions about your own document

**Copilot in Excel:**
- "What trends do you see in this data?"
- "Create a formula that calculates [description]"
- "Generate a chart showing [specific relationship]"
- "Which rows are anomalies and why?"
- "Summarise what this spreadsheet shows in plain English"

Note: Unlike ChatGPT's Code Interpreter (which runs Python), Excel Copilot works within Excel's native formula and chart system. It's less flexible for custom analysis but more integrated.

**Copilot in Outlook:**
- "Summarise this email thread and tell me what I need to respond to"
- "Draft a reply to this email that: [your requirements]"
- "What action items am I responsible for from today's emails?"
- "Schedule a meeting with these attendees about [topic], draft the invite"

**Copilot in Teams:**
- During a meeting: real-time note-taking
- After a meeting: "What were the key decisions made? What are my action items?"
- Catch up on a meeting you missed: AI-generated summary and recording transcript
- Chat summarisation: "Summarise what was discussed in this channel last week"

**Copilot in PowerPoint:**
- "Create a presentation about [topic] for a [audience] audience, [N] slides"
- "Add a slide summarising [key point]"
- "Improve the design of this slide"
- "Write speaker notes for this slide"

## Copilot vs. Gemini for Workspace Integration

If you use Google Workspace, Gemini is better. If you use Microsoft 365, Copilot is better. This is the clearest tool-choice rule in the AI landscape.

| Feature | Microsoft 365 Copilot | Gemini for Google Workspace |
|---------|----------------------|-----------------------------|
| Email | Outlook integration | Gmail integration |
| Documents | Word integration | Google Docs integration |
| Spreadsheets | Excel integration | Google Sheets integration |
| Presentations | PowerPoint integration | Google Slides integration |
| Meetings | Teams integration | Google Meet integration |
| Cost | ~£25-30/user/month add-on | Included in Google One AI Premium |
| Model | GPT-5.x | Gemini 2.5 Pro |
| Web search | Bing integration | Google Search integration |

**The correct advice:** Don't fight this. If your company uses Microsoft 365, learn Copilot — it's where your data already lives and where your colleagues are working. If you use Google Workspace personally or professionally, learn Gemini. The 10% capability difference between the tools matters far less than working within your existing stack.

**Copilot in Edge is free and available right now.** Every Windows computer has Edge installed, and Copilot in Edge requires no account and no payment. If you haven't tried it, open Edge, navigate to any long article, and click the Copilot icon. You have an AI research assistant alongside every web page you visit — at zero cost. This is the easiest AI tool win available to any Windows user.

**Not on Windows or don't use Edge?** Most Copilot features are available at [copilot.microsoft.com](https://copilot.microsoft.com) in any browser on any platform — Mac, Linux, Chrome, Firefox. The sidebar integration described below is Edge/Windows-specific, but the workshop can be completed at copilot.microsoft.com by pasting the article text into the chat instead of using the sidebar.

sections.title: Copilot in Edge — Research + Write Workflow
sections.content:
This workshop demonstrates the full research-to-writing workflow using only Copilot in Edge.

**Step 1 — Open Edge and find a long article**
Open Microsoft Edge and navigate to any substantive news article or web page — something with 500+ words of real content. (Wikipedia works well for this exercise.)

**Step 2 — Open the Copilot sidebar**
Click the Copilot icon (top right of Edge window) or press **Ctrl+Shift+.**. The sidebar opens alongside the page.

**Step 3 — Research mode: interrogate the page**
Type these prompts one at a time in the sidebar:
```
Summarise this page in 5 bullet points.
```
```
What claims in this page should I fact-check? List them.
```
```
What important questions does this page leave unanswered?
```

Observe: Copilot reads the page automatically. You didn't copy anything.

**Step 4 — Compose mode: produce something from it**
Click the **Compose** tab at the top of the Copilot sidebar (next to Chat).

Choose:
- Format: Email
- Length: Short
- Tone: Professional

In the "What do you want to write about?" box, type:
```
Share the key points from this article with my team and explain why it's relevant to [your topic/work]
```

Click Generate. Copy the result into your email client or a notes app.

**Step 5 — Compare to Claude**
Open [Claude.ai](https://claude.ai) in a new tab. Paste 3-4 paragraphs from the article and ask the same summarisation question.

Write down:
- What was different about working within the browser vs. switching to Claude?
- Which experience felt more natural for this type of task?
- In what work scenario would you reach for Copilot in Edge over Claude?

**Bonus: If you have Microsoft 365**
Open Word, Excel, or Outlook and look for the Copilot icon in the ribbon. Try asking it to summarise the document you're in, or draft a reply to an email you've been putting off.

sections.question: Your company uses Microsoft 365 and is deciding whether to pay for the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on. What is the strongest argument for paying for it vs. just having employees use free Claude or ChatGPT?
options: Microsoft 365 Copilot produces higher quality output than Claude
Microsoft 365 Copilot is cheaper than Claude Pro per user
Microsoft 365 Copilot works inside the tools where work actually happens (Outlook, Word, Teams) and can access company data in those documents — Claude and ChatGPT can't do that without copy-pasting
Microsoft 365 Copilot is the only tool that can summarise emails
sections.explanation: The decisive advantage is native integration with company data and existing workflow. Microsoft 365 Copilot can read your actual email threads in Outlook, your real documents in Word, and your meeting recordings in Teams — without employees having to copy and paste sensitive content into a third-party service. This data residency and workflow integration argument is the core enterprise case. Claude and ChatGPT can do equivalent tasks, but only when employees manually copy content to them — which is slower, creates data risk, and doesn't scale across an organisation.

sections.title: Workshop A — Microsoft Copilot First Tasks
sections.content:
Microsoft Copilot runs in Windows, Edge, and Bing. This drill tests it in your actual environment.

**Step 1 — Open Microsoft Copilot** in the way most accessible to you: the Copilot button in Windows 11, the Copilot sidebar in Edge browser, or copilot.microsoft.com.

**Step 2 — Test Copilot in Edge sidebar:** Navigate to a webpage relevant to your work. Open the Copilot sidebar and ask: "Summarise this page in 5 bullet points" and "What questions does this page not answer that I would need to know?"

**Step 3 — Test web-connected answers:** Ask Copilot about something current in your industry. Does it cite sources? How current is the information?

**Step 4 — Test image generation:** Ask Copilot to generate an image (it uses DALL-E 3). Request something work-related.

**Step 5 — Compare to Claude:** Ask the same question you used in step 2 in Claude.ai. Which gave more useful analysis?

sections.title: Workshop B — Complete a Real Work Task with Copilot
sections.content:
Use Microsoft Copilot to complete a task you actually need done this week.

**Step 1 — Choose a task** that suits Copilot: something that benefits from web-connected responses, involves browsing a web page, or is a Microsoft-ecosystem task.

**Step 2 — Run the task** through Copilot. Work through the conversation until you have a usable output.

**Step 3 — Evaluate the output:** Is it accurate? Is it formatted in a way you can use? Did it miss anything important?

**Step 4 — Mandatory review:** Paste the output to Claude.ai and say: *"Review this output. I'm using it for [describe your task]. Find 3 specific problems, gaps, or inaccuracies I should fix before using it."* Implement at least one fix.

**Step 5 — Record your comparison:** Is Microsoft Copilot better than Claude or ChatGPT for this type of task? Under what conditions would you choose Copilot over the others?

**Step 6 — Update your AI tools guide** with your Copilot findings.

sections.title: Workshop C — Copilot vs Claude on a Business Writing Task
sections.content:
Compare how Microsoft Copilot and Claude approach professional writing.

**Step 1 — Choose a real business writing task:** Draft an email, write a summary, produce a report section, create a meeting agenda.

**Step 2 — Run the task in Microsoft Copilot first.** Note the response quality, length, tone, and any formatting.

**Step 3 — Run the same task in Claude.** Note differences in approach.

**Step 4 — Evaluate both outputs against these criteria:**
- Which is closer to your actual professional tone?
- Which requires less editing before use?
- Which misunderstood the task more?
- Which would be more appropriate to share with your actual audience?

**Step 5 — Ask Claude** to compare both outputs: *"Here are two AI responses to a business writing task [paste both]. What are the key differences in approach and quality? For professional business writing in [your context], which approach is more appropriate and why?"*

sections.title: Workshop D — Add Copilot to Your Daily Windows Workflow
sections.content:
If you work on Windows 11, Copilot can be embedded in your daily routine without switching apps.

**Step 1 — Set up Copilot access:** Enable it in your Windows taskbar (if not already visible). Pin the Edge Copilot sidebar to your browser.

**Step 2 — Identify 2-3 daily tasks** that you could run through Copilot without switching apps: summarising a web page you're reading, drafting a quick email, searching for information while staying in your browser.

**Step 3 — Test each task** using Copilot in the sidebar or Windows panel rather than opening a separate AI tab.

**Step 4 — Rate the convenience:** Is in-context Copilot faster than switching to a dedicated AI tab? For which tasks?

**Step 5 — Decide:** Will you use the embedded Copilot as your quick, in-context AI, with dedicated Claude or ChatGPT for heavier tasks? Write your personal workflow rule.

sections.question: What is the main advantage of Microsoft Copilot over Claude for many Microsoft 365 users?
options: It produces higher quality writing than Claude
It is more accurate and less prone to hallucination
It integrates directly into Windows, Edge, and Microsoft 365 apps without switching applications
It is faster to respond than other AI tools
sections.explanation: Copilot's main advantage is seamless integration into the Microsoft ecosystem — it works inside Windows, Edge browser, Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, and other M365 apps. This reduces context switching. It's not necessarily better at writing or accuracy than Claude; the advantage is workflow integration for Microsoft-heavy users.

sections.question: You are reading an important 20-page report in your Edge browser and want a quick summary. What is the fastest approach?
options: Copy the entire report and paste it into Claude.ai
Open the Copilot sidebar in Edge and ask it to summarise the current page
Download the PDF and upload it to ChatGPT
Read it manually — AI summaries may miss key details
sections.explanation: The Edge Copilot sidebar can read and summarise the current page without copying or downloading anything — it's the fastest option for web-based documents. Claude is excellent for deep analysis once you have the content, but requires you to paste or upload the text. Copilot's in-browser integration is its biggest practical advantage for everyday page reading tasks.

sections.content: **You've completed lesson 2-6.** You understand the full Copilot map — from the free browser sidebar to enterprise M365 integration — and when to use Copilot vs. Gemini vs. Claude. For Windows users: Copilot in Edge is free, available now, and already proves its value on the first long article you read with it.
